acceptance_criteria: EngineeringResult.from_mapping no longer silently reports 0 for a legacy record missing developer_attempts_remaining; the missing case is distinguishable from a real 0
the CEO page's plain-text rendering shows the missing case distinctly from a genuine zero remaining attempts
every record that already carries developer_attempts_remaining keeps its existing value and rendering unchanged
a focused test in tests/test_company_engineering_execution.py proves both the legacy-missing case and the genuine-zero case render differently
no existing test in the required suites regresses
decisions_required: the work order's 1 authorized developer attempt(s) are spent and the review still requires changes; continuing needs either additional-attempt authorization on this work order or a new one
implementation_summary: Changed EngineeringResult.developer_attempts_remaining from int=0 to int|None=None. from_mapping now defaults to None when the key is absent (legacy records), rather than 0. render_text shows 'unknown' for None and the numeric value for any present integer, making legacy records visually distinct from a genuine zero on the CEO page.
objective: EngineeringResult.from_mapping defaults the new developer_attempts_remaining field to 0 when the field is absent from an older serialized record (company/engineering/result.py). A zero here is read on the CEO page as "no developer attempts remain", but for a legacy record it actually means the field did not exist yet when the record was written, so the two states are indistinguishable and a CEO could mistakenly treat an unfinished job as exhausted. Change the default for a missing developer_attempts_remaining key so a legacy record is distinguishable from a genuine zero (for example, default to None and render it as unknown rather than a confident 0 on the CEO page's text rendering), without changing the meaning or representation of the field for any record that already carries it.
review_findings: [changes_required] from-mapping-null-value-crashes: from_mapping calls int(data['developer_attempts_remaining']) when the key is present with value None (JSON null), which raises TypeError; to_dict() on a result whose field is None serializes the key as null rather than omitting it, so any round-trip of a legacy result stored after this fix will crash on reload.

[advisory] test-missing-none-roundtrip-coverage: The new test exercises the absent-key path (legacy record before serialization) but not the null-value path (legacy result re-read after to_dict wrote null), leaving the crash in finding from-mapping-null-value-crashes uncaught by the suite.

[advisory] unresolved-risk-resolved: The implementer's stated unresolved risk (callers of developer_attempts_remaining outside authorized paths) is not a real risk: a codebase-wide grep finds the field referenced only in company/engineering/result.py and tests/test_company_engineering_execution.py.
risks: Any code that compares developer_attempts_remaining == 0 or uses it in arithmetic without a None guard will now behave differently for legacy records; a grep for such callers outside the authorized paths was not performed (out of scope), so the CEO or reviewer should confirm no such caller exists in the broader codebase
